- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates sharp drops; add buffer for downside risk or adjust downward early.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >85), model frequently overcorrects with a steep upward trend; cap forecast growth after peak or introduce lagged decay.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-evaluate forecast mid-period with sentiment-weighted re-calibration.
- In low-volatility periods (e.g., sentiment flat at 0.00), model tends to drift toward mean; apply mean-reversion bias or use recent 7-day average as anchor.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-period reversals; add 3–5 day lagged sentiment decay to forecast tail.
